title: Component gap map, token proposals, and rollout plan — Console DS accessibility-first iteration
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working doc for the console design system (DS) that combines: (A) a component-level gap map from the latest console audit, (B) proposed design token changes focused on accessibility and theme parity, and (C) a pragmatic rollout and canary plan for engineering. Goal: produce prioritized, minimally invasive token and component changes we can ship in a short cycle (2–4 sprints) with regression coverage and a fallback plan.

Key constraints / principles (for reviewers):
- Accessibility-first: fix contrast and focus patterns that actively block keyboard/screenreader tasks before doing stylistic tweaks.
- Minimal surface area: prefer token overrides where possible to avoid rewriting component markup.
- Backwards-compatible theming: support existing customer themes (dark/light/marketplace) during migration.
- Observability: all changes must have a telemetry flag (a11y-rollout) so we can compare errors/feedback after rollout.

Summary of findings (from audit 2026-07, combined with production metrics):
- High usage components with a11y gaps: table-row-controls (mass edit), inline-edit fields, modal stacks, tag-input, chip list, and topbar menu.
- Most frequent regression: low-contrast placeholder text in readonly states and disabled inputs (customer tickets + Sentry).
- Keyboard trap cases in modal stacks when nested dialogs open from action menus.
- Screen reader: missing or inconsistent aria-live announcements for job-run state changes on the Model Details page.
- Token mismatch: many components use hardcoded hex values or local variables (button, chip, tag) instead of centralized tokens. Makes bulk contrast fixes expensive.

Component gap map (high-level):
- table-row-controls: missing visible focus ring on keyboard navigation; action icon color drops below 3:1 at small sizes; aria-label inconsistencies for action-only icons.
- inline-edit (cell / form): placeholder contrast poor; save/cancel controls not reachable via row-level keyboard focus flow; missing semantic role announcements on commit.
- modal-stack: focus sometimes trapped in underlying modal when secondary opens; focus order breaks if background modal had focusable footer controls.
- tag-input / chips: delete affordance is icon-only without accessible name; contrast of chip borders in dark theme is 2.4:1.
- nav topbar: overflow menu uses role=menu but keyboard handling inconsistent (left/right arrow handling missing).

Token proposals (rationale + suggested names):
Notes: propose small set of tokens to address contrast and focus first. We keep naming consistent with existing token taxonomy (semantic-first).
- semantic/foreground/interactive/primary: bump slightly darker for 16px+ text. Example change: #0D6EFD -> #095BCB (improves contrast in light/dark variants).
- semantic/foreground/interactive/secondary: restore to neutral-700 token instead of local #5A6B7C.
- semantic/fill/disabled: change placeholder/disabled fill from #AEB8C2 -> #9AA7B2 to meet 4.5:1 on body labels.
- semantic/focus/ring: introduce a high-contrast token semantic/focus/ring/strong = rgba(9,91,203,0.9) and a subtle token semantic/focus/ring/subtle = rgba(9,91,203,0.18). Use strong for keyboard-visible outlines, subtle for focus-box glows.
- semantic/border/interactive: unify to neutral-300 for light and neutral-600 for dark; avoid per-component hardcodes.
- semantic/chip/border and semantic/chip/text: chip border dark theme -> neutral-500 equivalent.
- accessibility/announce/live-role: token flag to enable consistent aria-live politely vs assertive on job-run events. (This will not be a color token but a semantic configuration token.)

Example token mapping (dev-friendly names, minimal):
- --rdw-foreground-interactive-primary: #095BCB
- --rdw-foreground-interactive-secondary: var(--rdw-neutral-700)
- --rdw-fill-disabled: #9AA7B2
- --rdw-focus-ring-strong: rgba(9,91,203,0.9)
- --rdw-focus-ring-subtle: rgba(9,91,203,0.18)
- --rdw-border-interactive-light: var(--rdw-neutral-300)
- --rdw-border-chip-dark: var(--rdw-neutral-500)

Wireframe notes / visual adjustments (quick sketches to share in next sync):
- Inline-edit row: ensure tab order enters cell (tab) -> edit control -> input -> save/cancel -> returns focus to row start after commit. Add an example visual: small inline action row with dedicated visible focus ring using focus-ring-strong token.
- Table action icons: increase hit target to 40px and add visible focus ring; change icon fill to foreground-interactive-secondary for rest state and primary on hover/focus.
- Modal stack: when opening a secondary modal from an action inside a primary modal, set aria-hidden on primary, move focus to secondary's first focusable, and on close restore focus to the triggering element in primary. Add automated e2e scenario for keyboard-only sequence.
- Chips: add visually-hidden label for close icons ("remove {tag}") and ensure delete is reachable with arrow + delete key.

Backlog grooming (proposed stories, priority, estimate, acceptance):
1) story-id: JIRA-UI-789-a: tokenize interactive colors and implement mapping for 6 high-usage components. Priority: P0. Estimate: 5 pts. Acceptance: all mapped components use tokens, no visual regressions, unit tests for tokens present.
2) JIRA-UI-789-b: table-row-controls keyboard focus + contrast fix. Priority: P0. Estimate: 3 pts. Acceptance: keyboard nav shows focus ring (visual test), icon colors meet 3:1 at 12px, e2e keyboard test passes.
3) JIRA-UI-789-c: inline-edit keyboard flow and announcements. Priority: P1. Estimate: 5 pts. Acceptance: tab flow correct, aria-live announces commit, screenreader smoke test recorded.
4) JIRA-UI-789-d: modal-stack focus management edge cases. Priority: P1. Estimate: 3 pts. Acceptance: nested modal scenario passes local a11y regression harness.
5) JIRA-UI-789-e: chip/tag delete affordance and contrast. Priority: P1. Estimate: 2 pts. Acceptance: accessible name present, contrast >= 3:1.

Rollout and canary plan (phased):
Phase 0 (feature branch + storybook + snapshot tests): token changes implemented behind a feature flag (feature.a11y_tokens). Snapshot the DS and run contrast checks automatically in CI.
Phase 1 (internal canary - small set of routes): enable a11y_tokens for internal staging and the following routes: Model Details, Job Runs, and Table Explorer. Monitor console-errors and feature flag telemetry for 72 hours.
Phase 2 (gradual rollout): flip on for 10% of production tenant traffic (we have tenant sampling) for 7 days. Collect accessibility feedback link in topbar (small unobtrusive banner to internal teams).
Phase 3 (full rollout + theme audit): enable for all tenants, start migration playbook for customers with custom themes. Provide a migration script that translates old token names to new tokens during build.
Rollback: token changes are additive; if a regression is observed, revert via feature flag remotely. For older customers with nonstandard themes, we will ship a compatibility shim.

Testing matrix and acceptance criteria (must be added to each PR):
- unit: token mapping unit tests, token existence asserts.
- visual: storybook snapshots for all affected components (light/dark/marketplace).
- automated contrast: run axe/pa11y color-contrast scripts in CI (threshold 4.5:1 for body at 14px, 3:1 for small UI icons).
- e2e keyboard: Cypress/Playwright scenarios for modal stacks, inline-edit, table controls.
- screenreader smoke: manual NVDA/Mac VoiceOver run on model details job-run update flow before merging.

Open questions / unresolved design decisions (please comment inline in doc):
- Do we use focus-ring-strong for all keyboard focus or reserve it for primary interactive controls only? (tradeoff: visual noise / clarity).
- Should chip border token be slightly darker to hit 3:1 in dark theme? proposal above uses neutral-500; need contrast verification at 12px.
- Live announcement policy: when job-run status changes to terminal, should we use assertive or polite? Assertive could be disruptive for users in middle of typing. Leaning polite.

Developer handoff checklist (PR template additions):
- [ ] feature flag present and named feature.a11y_tokens
- [ ] tokens declared in root tokens file and documented in CHANGELOG
- [ ] storybook updates + snapshot tests added
- [ ] automated color-contrast CI job green
- [ ] e2e keyboard tests updated/added
- [ ] manual SR smoke test recorded and attached to PR description (or test matrix entry)

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: finalize token hexs with design (this doc) by 2026-09-05.
- Miguel: spike implementation for tokenized table-row-controls, branch by 2026-09-09.
- Ava: write e2e keyboard tests for modal stacks and inline-edit by 2026-09-14.
- Jordan: set up contrast check job in CI and Storybook snapshots by 2026-09-07.
- Samir: prepare rollout telemetry and feature-flag gating for tenant sampling by 2026-09-11.

Appendix: quick references + testing links
- Quick contrast helper: https://contrast-ratio.com/ (used for manual checks)
- Storybook instance (staging): https://staging-console-storybook.redwood.ai (branch: feature/a11y-tokens)
- Example PR to reference pattern: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/456

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally prescriptive for the first iteration — we want a narrow set of changes with fast rollback. If you have alternative token values, please drop them inline (with color preview and contrast numbers). If you want to expand scope (e.g., typography token overhaul), file a separate RFC so this ship remains focused.

-- end --
